titulo: Posso, and then whatever you want to do
subtitulo: One frame for the whole first hour — pay, wait, charge, leave the bag — because the rules change building to building and nobody tells you which
cena: The luggage belt has stopped, your pickup has not appeared, and there are four small decisions between you and being able to sit down.
frasePiso: Posso plus the thing you want to do. One frame, and the whole arrivals hall becomes answerable.

clique.desconto: Nobody handed you a different sentence for each counter in that hall. You kept one opening and changed only the action after it.
clique.piso: Next time you are unsure whether something is allowed, you will not guess and hope. You will ask in four words.

steps.pt: Your first hour is a run of small permissions. The rules change building to building, so the useful skill is asking, not knowing.
Here is the frame: posso, then the action. Can I — and then the job. Same opening every time.

steps.promptPt: At the airport bar you want water and all you have is plastic. Ask. Speak now.

steps.pt: Of course, even for a coffee.
The frame holds; only the action changes. Same four words, completely different problem.

steps.promptPt: The toilets are past a staffed barrier. Ask whether you may use them. Speak now.
Your pickup is late and you want a visible spot near staff. Ask. Speak now.

steps.pt: Si accomodi means go ahead, sit, help yourself. You will hear it constantly — it is a yes with a welcome attached.

steps.promptPt: Battery nearly dead, and there is a socket by the wall. Ask. Speak now.
You need both hands free at the desk. Ask about the suitcase. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can I leave the suitcase here?
And when the answer is no, it usually comes with the reason and the alternative. Listen past the no.

steps.es: Qui no, ma c'è il deposito bagagli al piano di sotto.
steps.pt: Not here, but there's left luggage on the floor below.
steps.tts: Qui no, ma c'è il deposito bagagli al piano di sotto.

steps.promptPt: Your eSIM is not connecting. Ask about the wifi. Speak now.
Open a question with the same frame, politely. Speak now.
They sorted you out. Thank them properly. Speak now.
steps.pt: Thank you very much, very kind.

steps.es: Posso pagare con la carta? Posso usare il bagno? Posso aspettare qui?
steps.pinyin: POS-so pa-GA-re kon la KAR-ta. POS-so oo-ZA-re eel BA-nyo. POS-so as-pet-TA-re kwee
steps.pt: Shadow the same opening through three different actions.
steps.tts: Posso pagare con la carta? Posso usare il bagno? Posso aspettare qui?

steps.pt: B06 done. Posso plus the action covers pay, toilet, wait, charge and bag — five problems, one frame, four words each.

secoes.corpo: Keep posso and replace only the verb after it. The infinitive never changes shape, which is what makes this the cheapest frame in the course.

exemplos.pt: Can I leave the suitcase here?

secoes.corpo: Literally 'make yourself comfortable', used for sit down, come in, go ahead, help yourself. Recognising it saves the half-second of hesitation that makes a simple permission feel complicated.
An Italian no at a counter usually arrives with the reason and the alternative attached — qui no, ma c'è… Stopping at the no means missing the part that solves your problem.

Whether you can pay by card, leave a bag or sit somewhere varies by building, by city and by hour. Memorising a rule gives you one answer; the frame gives you the answer everywhere, including in the places nobody wrote a guide about.

permissao: You do not need a different sentence for every counter in that hall. Posso, the action, and a level tone is a complete request anywhere in the building, and nobody there is grading how you phrased it.
espelho: Anyone navigating an unfamiliar airport at home already runs this exact triage without noticing — bag, money, toilet, somewhere to stand. The only new part here is doing it in four words that all start the same way.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You ask whether you can do something and get a no, so you thank them and walk away.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: It is not allowed here, so there is nothing else to say.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: At an Italian counter the no is very often only the first half — qui no, ma c'è… — with the reason and the alternative following immediately. Walking away on the no means leaving the useful half of the answer on the counter.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Stay for one more beat after the no. If nothing follows, ask where you can instead — the frame you already have covers it.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You get the left-luggage desk, the other entrance, the machine that takes cards — the thing you actually needed.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not when the no is clearly final and the person has already turned away — at that point pressing for an alternative reads as not accepting the answer.
